Subject: SummitCare MAP: hosting-mode recommendation & region gating

Rajiv —

Thanks again for the discussion this morning. Per our commitment on the call, attached is a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) oriented around the hosting decision and region gating so SummitCare can close on the deployment mode by end of August. Highlights:

- Decision window: Hosted (US) vs Dedicated (reserved EU pool) vs Private (on-prem) — target decision by 2026-08-30.
- Evaluation plan: 2-week POC on Hosted (US-East) with telemetry and latency snapshots; parallel proof of throughput on a Dedicated EU staging pool if EU data residency is required.
- Acceptance criteria: 99th percentile tail latency <= 300ms for conversational flows in US, and ≤ 450ms in EU; SOC 2 evidence and audit log export validated; regression test pass rate >= 98% on the shared prompt set.
- Next steps: SummitCare to confirm region/PHI constraints and procurement timeline; Redwood to provide cost delta (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and a scoped SOW for Dedicated setup.

Attachments: SummitCare-MAP-20260816.pdf (MAP + timeline), latency-comparison-us-eu-aug2026.xlsx (baseline estimates)

If this plan looks right I’ll schedule a short 30-min alignment next week with your procurement and infra leads.

—Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]

Jordan —

Thanks for the MAP. A few immediate clarifying Qs from our side:

1) PHI scope: initial plan is to keep only de-identified clinical metadata in the cloud. PII/PHI must remain in our on-prem vault for now. Does Redwood have a hybrid pattern where session KV or tokens can be pinned to Customer-managed KMS or kept on-prem?

2) EU data residency: our EU customers require EU processing for any identifiable data. If we go Hosted for speed, would routing to an EU Dedicated pool be automatic for flagged requests or would we need separate tenant config?

3) Pricing & procurement: our SOW owner wants clear committed cost for Dedicated (monthly) vs Hosted (usage) with an estimated 500k tokens/month baseline for Q4.

Can Monica or Neha loop in answers and a preliminary commercial sheet? Procurement wants to see it before the 24th.

—Rajiv
Director, Product Ops | SummitCare
procurement@summitcare.com

Subject: Re: SummitCare MAP: hosting-mode recommendation & region gating

Hi Rajiv —

Short answers on security/compliance and hybrid options:

- Hybrid KMS: Yes. Redwood Private and Dedicated support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK). For Hosted we offer per-customer envelope encryption with Bring-Your-Own-Key on dedicated plans; for Hosted standard tier we manage keys but can enable customer keys on an enterprise addendum.
- On-prem KV: We offer an optional KV proxy for session tokens so sensitive keys can be vaulted on-prem while the runtime calls a secure endpoint. That is how several customers keep raw PHI out of cloud storage.
- EU routing: We can configure routing policies that map request attributes (customer_id, data_class) to region-specific pools. That requires Dedicated or Private for guaranteed residency; Hosted can do region filtering but not full tenancy isolation by default.

I’ve attached a brief security note and the SOC 2 artifacts we can share under NDA. We can walk the infra team through the KV proxy architecture in the technical POC.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SummitCare MAP: hosting-mode recommendation & region gating

Rajiv —

Adding a technical note on latency/throughput tradeoffs and what we typically see:

- Hosted (US-East): fastest path for US traffic, lower upfront commitment, predictable median latency ~80–120ms on short chat turns; 99th percentile depends on burst control but typically under 300ms for conversational sequences under 512 tokens.
- Dedicated (EU pool): provides tenancy isolation and predictable tail behavior — recommended if EU residency or tighter SLAs are required. We can reserve a pool (4x A100 equiv) scoped to your Q4 baseline; warm-up and cache priming will matter for 99th percentile.
- Private/on-prem: best for keeping any PHI on-prem, but requires infra ops work — typically 4–6 week rollout (install, network, KMS integration).

Proposed technical evaluation approach inside the MAP:
1) Week 1–2: Hosted POC in US-East — smoke tests, latency snapshots, prompt regression.
2) Parallel (optional): spin a Dedicated EU staging environment and run the same suite (throughput & residency checks).
3) If PHI gating is required after POC, plan a Private pilot for sensitive tenants.

I attached a small latency workbook with regional estimates. Happy to run a quick 30-min latency walkthrough with your infra team.

—Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[attachment: latency-comparison-us-eu-aug2026.xlsx (XLSX, 42KB)]

Rajiv / Procurement team —

Attached is a high-level commercial comparison (hosted vs dedicated vs private) based on the 500k tokens/month Q4 baseline you mentioned. Top-line:

- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): lower initial cost, variable month-to-month; estimated $0.025 per 1k tokens (net after pilot credits) — projected ~$12.5k/month at 500k tokens.
- Dedicated (reserved): monthly commit model; example for a 4x A100-equivalent reserved pool we estimate $45k–55k/month including managed ops; lower per-token when util is high and provides tenancy SLA.
- Private (on-prem): one-time deployment/installation + annual license; initial setup ~ $120k–160k + ops; lower per-token if you fully amortize infra but much longer runway.

Procurement asks: please confirm whether SummitCare can accept monthly reserved pricing and whether you need an enterprise addendum for BYOK. I can convert these to a draft SOW/quote if you confirm target mode and region.

—Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-cost-approx.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]
